newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dairy to be part of "Santer" package - Fischler.
newsitem.headline: Dairy to be part of "Santer" package - Fischler.

text.p: Dairy reform will be part of a package measures on agriculture and other sectors due to be presented by European Commission President Jacques Santer, EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Tuesday.
The so-called Santer package, expected in mid-July, will follow the conclusion an inter-governmental conference reviewing the EU treaty at a summit meeting in Amsterdam in June.
"Dairy will be part of the Santer package," Fischler told a news conference after three days of informal talks on future dairy policy after production quotas expire in March 2000.
Fischler said the package would contain only general principles with specific proposals following in the autumn.

The package is expected to consist of four main elements: - Budget guidelines from 1999 to 2005 for agriculture and other sectors. - Reform of EU structural funds for regional, social and agricultural development. - Impact on agricultural and other policies of EU expansion eastwards to include up to 10 new countries. - Guidelines for EU agricuultural reforms, notably in the cereals and beef sectors.
Fischler said that reform of the cereals and beef sectors, where large surpluses are forecast, would be much more substantial than in the dairy sector where only minor changes are expected.
The European Commission is due next month to publish a detailed report on the situation and outlook in the cereals sector.
Similar reports have already been issued on beef and dairy in preparation for reform proposals.
